prompt:
Create a complete seamless wildlife visitor cycle in ONE consistent sprite sheet. IMAGE 2 is canonical fine pixel-art squirrel, moss branch and right foliage. Preserve its warm daylight, tiny crisp pixel clusters, muted red fur and environmental proportions. NO oversized mascot, no thick black outline. EXACTLY SIX columns and FOUR rows = 24 cells, row-major, canvas3072x2048, each cell512x512. Flat solid magenta background #FF00FF, no text, numbers, grid, labels, shadows or extra objects. Every frame contains identical complete narrow branch and right-side leafy screen. All visible pixels including branch/leaves inside x40..470,y100..440 of each cell. Fixed camera, fixed cell canvas, fixed branch at y370. Squirrel neutral skull width65px body height150px (ears to feet), neutral foot center x220 y370; tail behind to left. Same anatomy and size THROUGHOUT, no enlarging head/body when walking. Branch foliage stationary across all 24 frames, not individually reframed. At runtime cell is 120px, visitor is small.
IMPORTANT: show a real ENTRY from BEHIND RIGHT LEAVES. Do not start with a visible squirrel. Step by step row-major:
1 branch+leaves ONLY, squirrel COMPLETELY hidden.
2 only nose tip peeks LEFT from leaf edge.
3 nose and one eye show; body hidden.
4 head and ears peek LEFT, shoulders hidden.
5 front paw reaches left onto bough, shoulders emerge.
6 both front paws reach left and pull; hind legs/tail still hidden.
7 chest crawls left, torso half emerging.
8 torso emerges, one hind paw steps onto branch, tail still partly behind leaves.
9 walking LEFT, second hind paw emerges; tail follows.
10 at perch x220, lowers hindquarters and curls tail on left.
11 turns head and body from left to right through a three-quarter FRONT-facing pose.
12 seated calmly at x220, nose RIGHT, tail LEFT.
13 seated same pose, gentle blink.
14 same position, eyes open and ears attentive.
15 starts leaning toward RIGHT leaves; front paw reaches right.
16 standing to move RIGHT, alternating articulated paws.
17 moves halfway to right leaf screen, paws gripping branch.
18 nose and head enter leaves, hindquarters still visible.
19 shoulders occluded, tail and hindquarters visible.
20 body mostly behind foliage, hind paw still visible.
21 only bushy tail curling behind foliage.
22 only tail tip visible at leaf edge.
23 tail almost completely hidden, only tiny tip.
24 branch+leaves ONLY, pixel-identical to FRAME1. No visible fur, tail, eyes or paws.
Maintain small travel increments, physically forward walking in the direction of travel, no reversed playback. Scenery exact same position/size, real intermediate joints. Fixed world scale and pixel density, not big tight character panels. Frame1 and24 must MATCH so loop restart has no pop. Do NOT put any already-standing animal in first frame. Do not depict entry by fading, scaling, transparency or copying a translated pose.

PRODUCTION CONSISTENCY CONTRACT (applies to every asset): Declare exact output canvas dimensions, equal cell dimensions when using a sprite grid, intended in-scene footprint, fixed projection/camera, light direction, pixel-cluster density and outline weight matching the scene reference. For animated subjects, lock the same model sheet across ALL actions: constant skull width, head-to-body ratio, torso length, costume seams, foot spacing and ground-contact baseline. First and last neutral poses must match the canonical idle geometry. Frame bounding boxes may grow only for moving limbs/props, NEVER enlarge or shrink the whole body to fill a cell. Use one common padded canvas; reserve at least 8 percent margins around the widest action, never crop ears/tail/furniture. No per-frame zoom, reframing, translation of a copied pose, squash/stretch, or automatic tight framing. Fixed props and furniture remain the same size and at the same anchors throughout. Define body height, head width, foot-center X and foot baseline Y numerically in each animation task. For scenes/UI/items, explicitly preserve aspect ratio, safe area, optical size, border thickness and reference pixel density across variants. Backgrounds fill all edges; UI nine-slice corners remain fixed; no baked-in labels or text. Inspect transition between idle and interaction, NOT just individual sheets. Size/anchor/style mismatch means reject and regenerate; a successful HTTP response is not visual approval. For visitors entering or leaving a scene, create an explicit approach/peek/emerge/settle sequence and a physically occluded exit. Start and end the complete loop in the SAME hidden state. Specify separate entry and exit directions: never replace entrance with reversed exit, fading, scaling, or a cut from invisible to a fully visible idle character. Validate the loop boundary as carefully as individual frames.
